components.rationale: Composite supplied: the three GOAL subcomponents are each covered; theorem thm:p02-fol-clausal-form (SUP 116-125) carries status proved=annex:p2.fol.clausal.composition and annex item ANX 107-176 writes every step of the composition proof, so the original note 'currently left to an exercise' is superseded by a written proof rather than lost; hypotheses (sentence input, nonempty-domain semantics, AC only for the forward direction) are stated.

Declared input is a first-order L-sentence (SUP 117); the complete pipeline NNF -> rectified NNF -> prenex NNF -> universal Skolem sentence -> CNF matrix -> clause set is stated in the theorem by reference to Table tab:p02-fol-normal-form-pipeline (CNF branch; step 6 marked comparison only) and the figure, and the annex proof traverses every stage; the example (SUP 237-239) states that an open formula needs a declared closure first.

Composition written in ANX 109-140: NNF/rectification/prenex introduce no nonlogical symbol and draw fresh binders from a fixed infinite enumeration (ANX 116-118; INH 101-118 binders outside V; table row 2); the Skolem step yields signature L* with one fresh function symbol per existential prefix position, arity-zero constants for initial existentials, terms over preceding universals only, finitely many (ANX 121-129; INH 284-301); the CNF/clause step Cl(theta) stays in L*, introduces no variable or symbol and no Tseitin symbols (ANX 135-140; SUP 96-98, 112; table rows 5, 7).

Directions stated correctly: an L-model of sigma expands (AC) to a model of the Skolem/clause side; the reduct of any S-model satisfies sigma without choice (SUP 119-121; INH 320-328; ANX 130-133, 165-171); only the Skolem step weakens same-signature equivalence (SUP 123-124; table row 4 'not same-signature formula equivalence'; figure caption; INH 432-435; ANX 173-174); the clause-set step is a same-models relation via universal closures, not formula-string equivalence (SUP 166-169, 203-206, 215-216); Tseitin flagged as only equisatisfiable (SUP 160-161). Expansion/reduct defined SEM 22-40; reduct invariance proved RED 69-90. No formula equivalence is asserted where only satisfiability transfer holds.
